action: Braiins advises miners to remove every stratum+tcp:// entry, including backups, and use Stratum V2 or TLS on firmware that verifies certificates; it tells network operators to turn on RPKI route origin validation.
date_note: Braiins' post is dated 25 Nov and reports attack waves from 7 to 20 Nov; the post gives no earlier single day for the disclosure.
exec: Braiins says miners on plain-text Stratum V1 can have their hashrate silently redirected to an attacker.
impact: Braiins says its own systems and pool accounts were not compromised.
org: Bitcoin mining sites on Stratum V1
plain: Braiins says an attacker rerouted internet traffic so miners' computing power went to a fake mining pool, and the rewards went to the attacker. It says miners using unencrypted connections are exposed.
summary: Bitcoin mining firm Braiins says an attacker used BGP route manipulation to impersonate mining pools to miners on plain-text Stratum V1, so their hashrate was diverted to a fake server. Braiins says the attacks came in waves from early November, starting in Latin America and reaching Europe, and one hit more than a thousand mining sites in the same second. Braiins says neither the miners' ASICs nor Braiins Pool were compromised.
title: Braiins reports bitcoin hashrate hijacking through BGP route manipulation of unencrypted Stratum V1 connections

validation.note: Braiins' own post was read; The Block and Decrypt report the same findings from Braiins. The attacker and the amount of rewards stolen are not stated in the pages read.

evidence.quote: more than a thousand mining sites
